headline: Expelled Jamaat MP Gazi Nazrul Islam gets anticipatory bail in murder attempt case
summary: The High Court granted eight weeks of bail to the Satkhira-4 MP after a case was filed by his driver, who is also the uncle of the MP's second wife.
details: The High Court has granted eight weeks of anticipatory bail to Gazi Nazrul Islam, the MP for Satkhira-4, who was expelled from Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami.
caption:
Expelled Jamaat MP Gazi Nazrul Islam has been granted eight weeks of anticipatory bail by the High Court in an attempted murder case.

headline: Govt undecided on PM's attendance at BRICS summit
summary: Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman says no decision has been made regarding Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's visit to New Delhi for the summit.
details: The government has not yet decided whether Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will attend the BRICS summit in New Delhi on September 12-13.

Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman stated that no decision has been taken on whether to accept invitations for a bilateral visit from Indian PM Narendra Modi or for the BIMSTEC chairperson to attend the BRICS summit.

During a courtesy call by Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi, the two sides discussed the extradition of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina and the return of suspects involved in the killing of Inquilab Moncho spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi.
Bangladesh has urged India to expedite the extradition of Sheikh Hasina and has provided documents regarding the suspects of Hadi's killing.
The foreign minister mentioned that Bangladesh had clearly conveyed its position to New Delhi regarding an address by Hasina on August 5.
He expressed reassurance that Indian authorities have understood the seriousness of the issue and that such incidents would not be repeated.
The meeting also briefly touched upon recent border killings and push-ins, while river management and the Ganges Water Sharing Treaty were not discussed.
caption:
Will the Prime Minister visit India for the BRICS summit? The government says no decision has been made yet.

The government has not yet decided whether Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will attend the BRICS summit in New Delhi on September 12-13.

Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman stated that no decision has been taken on whether to accept invitations for a bilateral visit from Indian PM Narendra Modi or for the BIMSTEC chairperson to attend the BRICS summit.

During a courtesy call by Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi, the two sides discussed the extradition of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina and the return of suspects involved in the killing of Inquilab Moncho spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi.

Bangladesh has urged India to expedite the extradition of Sheikh Hasina and has provided documents regarding the suspects of Hadi's killing.

The foreign minister mentioned that Bangladesh had clearly conveyed its position to New Delhi regarding an address by Hasina on August 5.

He expressed reassurance that Indian authorities have understood the seriousness of the issue and that such incidents would not be repeated.

The meeting also briefly touched upon recent border killings and push-ins, while river management and the Ganges Water Sharing Treaty were not discussed.
